rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: San Francisco landlords may not use algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy. Tenants can sue for damages, an injunction and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and each month of use for each affected unit can count as a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each unit-month may be a separate violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential dwelling units in San Francisco using qualifying algorithmic devices
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance prohibits landlords from using qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy.
rules.penalty: Damages, injunctive relief, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month of use per affected unit may be a separate violation (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C(b), (d))

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: San Diego landlords may not use algorithmic rent-setting products of the kind the ordinance prohibits. Tenants can sue for damages, an injunction and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and each month and each affected rental property can count as a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; per month and per property
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in San Diego
rules.quoted_span: San Diego similarly authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and affected rental property potentially constituting a separate violation.
rules.penalty: Damages, injunctive relief, penalties up to $1,000 per violation (San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.1103(b), 98.1104(a))

rules.title: Ban on coordinated rent-pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not use coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents. Each unit and each month of use can count as a recurring violation, and tenants have private remedies.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental units in Berkeley
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms; recurring unit/month violations and private remedies, previously at issue in
rules.conflict_note: RealPage challenged the ordinance in RealPage, Inc. v. City of Berkeley (N.D. Cal.). The source says that case was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on Jan. 14, 2026, so the ordinance appears to stand.

rules.title: Ban on automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: Santa Ana landlords may not use the types of automated rent price-fixing the ordinance names. Tenants can sue for up to $1,000 per violation, counted per month.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental units in Santa Ana
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.penalty: Private tenant claims; up to $1,000 per violation and per month

rules.title: Ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Jersey City landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. Both the city and private parties can enforce the ban, with fines of up to $2,000 per day.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental units in Jersey City
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.penalty: Fines up to $2,000 per day; public and private enforcement

rules.title: Ban on software/algorithmic coordination of rents
rules.requirement: Hoboken landlords may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental units in Hoboken
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.

notes:
The source is a secondary law-firm LawFlash from Morgan Lewis, dated Aug. 21, 2026, so confidence is lowered for every record. The effective dates come from a summary table, and most give only a month.

Left out because they are outside the jurisdictions in scope: Seattle, King County, Spokane, Philadelphia, Minneapolis, Providence, Portland, Rockville (not yet effective, Jan. 1, 2027), and the pending proposals in Montgomery County MD, Evanston IL and Rhode Island.

Other points for review:
- The article calls the SF/San Diego actions "county-level," but the ordinances it cites are city ordinances.
- Hoboken: the citation "ch. 158-2" is copied as published and is unusual, so it should be checked. No penalty is given.
- The article does not mention any California or New Jersey state law on algorithmic rent setting. It says only in general terms that the authority of these local ordinances may be challenged. I did not flag a specific preemption conflict because the document gives no basis for one.
- None of the summaries give unit-count or building-age coverage tests.
